html:
Mswati II was king of the Swazi from about 1840 until 1868, the greatest of the fighting kings, after whom the Swazi and Swaziland were named.

Son of Sobhuza I, he organised the young men into national age regiments on the Zulu model, raided neighbours for cattle and captives, and pushed the kingdom's borders north. He strengthened the king's rituals, above all the Incwala.

He sought British support against the Zulu and made deals with the Boers, ceding land to the Transvaal. His people came to be called Swazi, the people of Mswati. The kingdom he left was strong, but his successors lost much of it through the concessions of the 1880s, before Sobhuza II won it back in part.
sum: Mswati II was king of the Swazi from about 1840 until 1868, the greatest of the fighting kings, after whom the Swazi and Swaziland were named.
